hypothesis: Light eth_call is wakeup-bound; leaving C6/C6P costs 170-210us on c8i and C2 100us on c8a. Disabling idle states with exit latency above 1us (keeps POLL and C1) should cut wakeup latency on x86. c8g exposes no cpuidle states, so it doubles as a control there.
llm_commentary: Disabling C2 (100us exit latency, acpi_idle; verified disable=1 on-box) on m8azn.xlarge is neutral: 5.51s → 5.50s on the same boot. It has the same C2 state as c8a, where turning it off gives ~2-3%, but here the node and the oha client share only 4 vCPUs, so cores rarely idle long enough to enter C2 during the run and there is little wake-up latency to save. The C2 lever pays off only where spare cores sit idle between wakeups (c8a's 8 vCPUs), and it is a no-op on the Graviton boxes, which expose no cpuidle states.
